step1_analysis.description: A high-speed current-mode logic (CML) circuit, likely a D-latch or a phase detector slice used in the clock and data recovery (CDR) or deserializer block. It features differential pairs and current source biasing, typical for Gb/s transceiver front-ends.

paper_reference.title: A 2.5–3.125-Gb/s Quad Transceiver With Second-Order Analog DLL-Based CDRs

power_consumption.description: Total DC power consumption of the subcircuit.

sky130_expected.calculation: Assuming 5 bias branches with ~1mA each at 1.8V supply.
sky130_expected.reasoning: The 32mW reported is for the entire transceiver. A single CML latch/buffer slice typically consumes 1-10mW depending on the tail currents.

voltage_swing.description: Peak-to-peak voltage swing at the output node.

sky130_expected.reasoning: CML circuits typically operate with reduced swings (200mV - 600mV) to maximize speed. With 1k pull-ups, swing depends on the exact bias current.

propagation_delay.description: Time delay from the input crossing to the output crossing.

sky130_expected.calculation: Simulated transient delay from INP to OUTP.
sky130_expected.reasoning: SKY130 (130nm) is comparable to the original paper's technology, so delays in the tens of picoseconds are expected for CML stages.

step3_testbench.description: Transient analysis to measure power consumption, voltage swing, and propagation delay of the CML circuit. Pull-up resistors are added to VDD since they are missing from the all-NMOS extracted netlist.

R2 OUTP VDD 1k
R3 N9 VDD 1k
R4 N11 VDD 1k

* Power Supplies
VVDD VDD 0 1.8
VVSS VSS 0 0

* Bias Voltages
VB23 N23 0 0.7
VB25 N25 0 0.7
VB22 N22 0 0.7
VB24 N24 0 0.7
VB21 N21 0 0.7
VB0 N0 0 1.2
VB18 N18 0 1.2
VB14 N14 0 1.2
VLABEL_NET_0 LABEL_NET_0 0 0.9
VLABEL_NET_1 LABEL_NET_1 0 0.9

* High-Speed Inputs (1.25 GHz)
VINP INP 0 PULSE(0.6 1.2 0 50p 50p 350p 800p)
VINM INM 0 PULSE(1.2 0.6 0 50p 50p 350p 800p)
VCLKP CLKP 0 PULSE(0.6 1.2 200p 50p 50p 350p 800p)

* Analysis
.control
tran 5p 5n

* 1. Power Consumption
meas tran power_avg avg i(VVDD)
let power_mw = -power_avg * 1.8 * 1000
print power_mw

* 2. Voltage Swing
meas tran v_max max v(OUTP) from=2n to=5n
meas tran v_min min v(OUTP) from=2n to=5n
let v_swing = v_max - v_min
print v_swing

* 3. Propagation Delay
meas tran t_in_cross trig v(INP) val=0.9 rise=3
meas tran t_out_cross targ v(OUTP) val=0.9 fall=3
let delay_ps = (t_out_cross - t_in_cross) * 1e12
print delay_ps

quit
.endc
.end
